ai.title: Elvis and Eminem rights holders are suing Suno
ai.brief: Suno is facing yet another pair of lawsuits . A group of rights holders of Elvis Presley’s music and the publisher of some of Eminem‘s biggest records are suing the AI music company, claiming it illegally generates music and lyrics that mimic those artists. The lawyers in the Presley suit claim that Suno has violated Tennessee’s Ensuring Likeness Voice and Image Security (ELVIS) Act, which makes it illegal for an AI company to clone a singer’s voice. “ These suits closely mirror one filed by Jason Isbell and others in September, which claimed Suno created imitations of the plaintiffs but did not claim copyright infringement directly. ”

sec.title: Iris Ohyama data cloud breach exposes info of 7.7 million customers
sec.brief: 7 million people may have been exposed after unauthorized access to a third-party cloud service the company used. The company discovered the incident late last month and publicly disclosed it with limited details, along with an announcement that the site would be temporarily suspended. In an update earlier this week, the company said it had discovered a suspicious file in an external cloud service used by the Iris Plaza online store. “We immediately suspended Iris Plaza and related systems and began an investigation. We confirmed unauthorized access by a third party and disclosed it in our first notice on October 29,” [machine translated] the company said . The investigation has confirmed that customer data stored in the compromised external cloud service may have been accessed by unauthorized actors. 9 million non-members.
